spec: DESIGN.md — firmware: an emulator-centric answer, live declarations against packaged identities
description: Whole fixture machines in; the canonical firmware serializations (atlas/contract.py firmware_contract, identification_contract) out, asserted with exact equality. A firmware answer is about EMULATORS: each installed core states what it wants, where each file goes as an absolute path, and what is actually lying there. Two axes stay apart — need (required/optional) is what an emulator asks for, checked (verified/mismatch/unchecked/unknown/not-comparable) is what the machine answers, and 'we did not look' never collapses into 'we looked and cannot tell'. The load-bearing pair is firmware-core-that-declares-nothing-answers-nothing-needed against firmware-core-not-installed-is-unknown-not-nothing: the same empty list, opposite meanings, and only the installed flag plus a caveat tells them apart. Firmware blobs are stated as {md5, sha1, size} because firmware is not text and its identity is exactly what a real file would answer with. A core's requirements list is a conjunction, and one entry may be an 'alternatives' group — a single-key object whose options are full requirements each carrying 'regions', the console regions whose launch it serves, disjoint across the group: one launch needs exactly one option, the running disc's region decides, and a region no option lists has nothing stated for it. A third axis joins them and never merges with either: supplied_by says WHOSE file is at the destination, and it is set exactly when the bytes there equal the bytes the distribution's own preparation step copies in (atlas/data/distribution_supplied.json). It is read whether or not verification was asked for, because a consumer deciding whether a file is safe to delete needs it on a cheap answer too, and it is null wherever nothing was established — not the distribution's copy, no copy list for this distribution, no entry for this destination.

vectors.rationale: The case that decides the model. Gambatte wants gb_bios.bin, SameBoy wants dmg_boot.bin, and the packaged table carries both under one md5. The bytes are on disk under Gambatte's name, so Gambatte verifies and SameBoy is genuinely missing — a byte-identical file under the other name does not satisfy it, because SameBoy opens dmg_boot.bin and nothing else. Each emulator answers with its whole declaration set, so the Game Boy Color boot ROMs come along carrying system=gbc rather than being silently dropped. identify_firmware then answers the download flow from the same fixture: one content, both destinations, so the client can say 'copy what you already have' instead of 'download this'.

A consumer working in RomM slugs that forgets to translate to the frontend's names lands exactly here. vectors.name: emudeck-firmware-a-broken-resource-shadow-claims-nothing
vectors.rationale: The firmware route over the same broken resource shadow the catalogue vector guarantees: the shadow is the file ES-DE loads instead of the embedded copy, so a shadow that exists and cannot be read means what the catalogue says is unknown — the firmware answer carries the unreadable-catalogue claim instead of enumerating emulators from the overlay alone. Locks in what a live probe established.

vectors.name: retrodeck-cemus-keys-are-a-packaged-expectation
vectors.rationale: A standalone emulator ships no .info, so what it expects is a packaged card, and the answer says so: declaration 'packaged' with the provenance caveat, never dressed up as a machine read. The destination is the emulator's own probe — Cemu reads its keys at GetUserDataPath('keys.txt') (KeyCache.cpp:63 at 2.6), the flatpak's data home here — resolved through the arrangement's symlink into the BIOS staging path, and what sits there is read live. No packaged identity can exist for a user-supplied key file, so a present file answers 'unknown' and stays honestly unverifiable.

vectors.name: emudeck-the-launcher-route-carries-the-keys-expectation
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck's catalogue names the launcher script, and the launcher route's word — variant-gated, exactly as the save route gates it — carries the same packaged card to the firmware answer. The destination is the AppImage's own probe on the host XDG tree (~/.local/share/Cemu/keys.txt), and here nothing sits at it: EmuDeck's installer parks a found keys.txt in the config directory instead (emuDeckCemu.sh), a path the shipped Linux build's key probe never reads — so the honest answer is a missing file at the door the emulator actually opens.

files./home/deck/.config/Cemu/keys.txt: # parked where the probe never looks

vectors.name: retrodeck-melonds-external-bios-makes-the-ds-set-required
vectors.rationale: melonDS ships no .info, so its expectations are atlas's packaged card — and which files a launch probes is verifySetup's own decision, read live from two switches (EmuInstance.cpp:633-667 at 1.1). With Emu.ExternalBIOSEnable on and the console type left at DS, the probe set is the ARM9/ARM7 BIOS pair and the DS firmware, each at the path its configuration key names — here RetroDECK's bios directory, where two of the three really sit and the third does not.

vectors.name: melonds-the-built-in-replacement-needs-no-external-bios
vectors.rationale: Emu.ExternalBIOSEnable is off — melonDS's compiled default — so DS games boot on the built-in BIOS/firmware replacement and verifySetup probes nothing at all. The empty requirement list is the true answer here, not an unread one, and the firmware-builtin-replacement caveat names the switch whose flip would make the configured DS paths required. The paths are configured in this fixture precisely to prove they are not read while the switch is off.

vectors.name: melonds-dsi-mode-needs-its-bios-pair-and-nand-either-way
vectors.rationale: The console type is the second switch, and it cuts across the first: in DSi mode the DSi BIOS pair and the NAND are probed whether or not external BIOS is on (verifySetup, EmuInstance.cpp:646-658) — only the DSi firmware rides the switch. With external BIOS off the answer therefore states three required files and still carries the built-in-replacement caveat, because that caveat is about the DS set.

vectors.name: melonds-an-unset-path-names-no-file-to-place
vectors.rationale: A probed key whose value names no file — unset, or ending in a directory step — is refused with the same word the core route refuses such a declaration with (firmware-path-names-no-file), never answered with the config directory dressed as a BIOS file: melonDS opens the relative spelling below its own config directory (Platform.cpp:157-178) and its check fails. The other two keys of the same probe set still answer, so a caller sees exactly which one is unconfigured.

vectors.name: melonds-an-unreadable-config-leaves-the-expectations-unknown
vectors.rationale: The configuration that decides which files are probed exists and cannot be read, so what this launch expects is unknown — declaration 'unreadable' with the save route's own word for the same fact (emulator-config-unreadable), and an empty list that says so rather than 'needs nothing'.

vectors.name: emudeck-melonds-parks-its-bios-paths-behind-a-switch-that-is-off
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck writes all seven melonDS path keys into the legacy INI it ships and leaves ExternalBIOSEnable=0 in the same file — so the paths are parked behind a switch that is off, and the honest answer names no DS requirement while saying which switch would create them. Two facts ride along: the launcher pins the flatpak variant (melonds.sh:4), so the expectations are read from the app's own config home below ~/.var/app rather than the host's; and the legacy INI is what melonDS 1.1 itself reads while no TOML exists.

vectors.name: retrodeck-pcsx2-has-nowhere-to-boot-from-until-a-bios-is-chosen
vectors.rationale: PCSX2's expectation takes two settings, not one: [Folders] Bios names the directory and [Filenames] BIOS the image inside it, and FullpathToBios composes nothing at all while the name is empty (Pcsx2Config.cpp:2057-2062 at v2.6.3). Empty is the shipped state — RetroDECK points the directory at its BIOS root and leaves the choice to the user — so this is not a broken configuration, but it does mean no game boots yet. The answer says so and names the directory a BIOS belongs in, rather than passing over it or inventing a file name.

vectors.name: retrodeck-pcsx2-states-the-bios-image-its-config-picked
vectors.rationale: With a name chosen the two settings compose one required file — the image inside the directory — and what sits there is read live. The name stays the one the configuration spelled rather than whatever symlinks end at, the rule every card-declared requirement follows.

vectors.name: retrodeck-pcsx2-a-sandbox-bios-directory-is-read-where-the-host-keeps-it
vectors.rationale: A flatpak emulator writes its configuration from inside its own sandbox, so the directory it names is a sandbox path: /var/config/PCSX2/bios is what the app sees, and the host reads the very same directory under ~/.var/app/net.retrodeck.retrodeck/config. The firmware route used to take such a value as a host path and report the BIOS missing while it was sitting there — the save route of this same emulator had always translated. Both now go through one map, so the two routes cannot disagree about where a configured directory lands.

vectors.name: retrodeck-pcsx2-a-bios-directory-only-the-sandbox-can-reach-is-said-not-guessed
vectors.rationale: The other half of the same map: /run/user/1000 is the sandbox's own private runtime directory, which names something else inside the app than it does out here, so no host path exists for it at all. That is not a missing BIOS — nothing was looked at — and the answer says exactly that with sandbox-path-untranslated rather than reporting a fault that may not be there.

vectors.name: pcsx2-a-chosen-bios-that-is-not-there-is-a-missing-required-file
vectors.rationale: The discriminating half of the pair: the configuration picked an image and nothing is at that path. That is a required file reported missing — a different fact from no image being chosen at all, and a client acting on the two would do different things.

vectors.name: pcsx2-a-relative-bios-directory-resolves-against-the-dataroot
vectors.rationale: [Folders] Bios goes through the same LoadPathFromSettings helper as the memory-card and texture directories (Pcsx2Config.cpp:2272-2278), so a relative value — the compiled default 'bios' among them — resolves against the DataRoot rather than against nothing.

vectors.name: pcsx2-an-unreadable-config-leaves-the-bios-expectation-unknown
vectors.rationale: The file that decides both the directory and the image exists and cannot be read, so what this launch expects is unknown — declaration 'unreadable' with the save route's own word for the same fact, and an empty list that says so rather than 'needs nothing'.

vectors.name: retrodeck-xemu-needs-three-files-and-generates-the-fourth
vectors.rationale: Five paths sit in xemu's [sys.files] and only three are firmware. The MCPX boot ROM, the flash image and the hard disk are the files xemu's own documentation calls necessary to run the emulator at all, and the shipped binary carries each one's failure message as a whole string — but of the three only the flash image's failure actually holds the launch, which is why the card states the consequence per file rather than once for all three. eeprom_path is left to the save answer on purpose: xemu generates an EEPROM where none exists, and it holds the console's own settings, which the standalone save card already states as a named settings group. dvd_path is the disc, which is content. The hard disk is claimed by both answers deliberately — xemu asks for one, and every save lives inside it.

vectors.name: xemu-an-empty-machine-setting-names-no-file-to-place
vectors.rationale: None of the five settings has a compiled default path (config_spec.yml:359-364 — plain strings, and a string with no default of its own compiles to the empty one), so an unset one names nothing at all. Each is refused by name with firmware-path-names-no-file rather than answered with an invented path, and each caveat says what that particular file's absence costs — the flash image is the one xemu will not start the console without.

vectors.name: xemu-an-unparseable-config-leaves-the-expectation-unknown
vectors.rationale: The file that names all three exists and does not parse, so what this launch expects is unknown — declaration 'unreadable' with the save route's own word for the same fact, and an empty list that says so rather than 'needs nothing'.

vectors.name: emudeck-xemu-reads-the-flatpaks-own-data-home
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck installs xemu as the app.xemu.xemu flatpak (emuDeckXemu.sh:4-5), so the launch's flatpak variant answers from the app's own homes below ~/.var/app — and xemu keeps its settings under the *data* home rather than the config one, which is why the read goes there. The names it finds are that arrangement's own: an installation may point the flash image at a differently named dump than another one does, which is exactly why the answer reads the configuration instead of listing known file names.

vectors.name: retrodeck-duckstation-searches-a-directory-and-recognises-the-image
vectors.rationale: DuckStation names no BIOS file: [BIOS] SearchDirectory names a directory, the three per-region keys are empty — the state RetroDECK ships — and the emulator keeps every file of an accepted size and recognises it by hashing it against a table compiled into the binary. Both files here are exactly 512 KiB, which is why the size test cannot be the answer: one is a PlayStation BIOS the table knows and the other is a Saturn image of the same size. The known one wins, because an unknown image never displaces a known one, and the answer names what it is rather than only where it is.

vectors.name: duckstation-an-image-the-table-does-not-know-still-boots
vectors.rationale: The directory holds one file of an accepted size and its bytes are in no row of the table. That is not a verdict against the file: the emulator boots it and says 'Using an unknown BIOS', so it is stated as the pick with its identity left unestablished. The one image recognised without a hash — the OpenBIOS replacement, by an eight-byte signature at a fixed offset — is named in the same caveat, because no read through atlas's seam reaches it.

vectors.name: duckstation-two-images-that-rank-alike-leave-the-pick-to-the-directory
vectors.rationale: Two images the table knows, both priority 5, both valid for a console of no stated region. Upstream keeps the last one the directory hands it, which makes the pick a property of readdir order rather than of the files — an order atlas cannot reproduce, since the seam enumerates sorted. So the tie is stated instead of resolved into a claim, and the requirement still names a file: one of them is there, and that is what the question 'can this boot' turns on.

data.reason: the console's region is the running disc's

vectors.name: duckstation-a-bios-whose-bytes-cannot-be-read-is-not-an-unrecognised-one
vectors.rationale: The search is a question about content, so a file whose bytes will not come back leaves it unanswered. The answer used to treat an unreadable image exactly like one that hashed cleanly and matched no row — 'its bytes are in no row of DuckStation's own table' — and then called the requirement satisfied: a verdict on bytes nobody read, and an all-clear on top of it. Now the read failure is stated as itself and no image is named as the one this launch would boot, which is the same shape this route takes when no content check was asked for at all.

vectors.name: duckstation-a-bios-directory-that-cannot-be-listed-holds-nothing-nobody-knows
vectors.rationale: The directory is there and its contents cannot be read. That establishes nothing about what is in it, so the answer states the failed listing and stops — it used to add that the directory 'holds no file of a size this emulator accepts', which is a claim about contents the failed listing never reached, and it read as a diagnosis ('put a BIOS here') for a machine whose real problem is a directory atlas cannot open.

vectors.name: duckstation-without-a-content-check-the-search-answers-nothing
vectors.rationale: The same machine, asked without verification. Which file is a BIOS is a question about bytes, and nothing was hashed, so the honest answer is the directory, the count of files whose size the emulator accepts, and no requirement at all — 'there is one here' would be a guess. The caveat's data names the regions the unanswered search speaks for — all three here, every key being empty. This is the shape of every unverified answer to a search card.

vectors.name: duckstation-a-directory-with-nothing-of-the-right-size-boots-nothing
vectors.rationale: The search directory is there and holds only files of sizes the emulator skips before reading a byte of them. Nothing names an image either, so there is no requirement to state and the caveat carries the directory a BIOS belongs in — the same shape PCSX2's empty [Filenames] BIOS answers with, because a PlayStation starts nothing until one is there.

vectors.name: duckstation-a-named-region-image-is-opened-where-the-setting-points
vectors.rationale: PathNTSCU names an image and the other two keys stay empty, and one launch reads exactly one of the region keys — the console region the running disc sets decides — so the answer is a single alternatives group, not two files both needed: the named file as the ntsc-u option, composed onto the search directory rather than read as a path of its own, and the search's find as the option of the two regions left to it. The named one is missing here, which is exactly the state a client needs to see — the search finding an image does not make the named path exist, and only a US console's launch lacks it.

vectors.name: duckstation-an-absolute-bios-image-name-joins-below-the-search-directory
vectors.rationale: The #320 witness, one machine for all three spellings of a region key. PathNTSCU is absolute — DuckStation composes every named image with Path::Combine(EmuFolders::Bios, bios_name) (bios.cpp:350 at stenzek/duckstation@64655818e), which swallows the value's leading separator and lands it BELOW the search directory, where atlas's os.path.join used to let the value replace the directory and name a file this emulator never opens. The image really sits at the composed path, so the requirement is satisfied there and nowhere else. PathNTSCJ carries a relative sub-path — the half the two joins agree on — composed below the same directory and missing there. PathPAL is empty, so the search speaks for the one region left to it and identifies the PAL image it finds.

vectors.name: duckstation-an-image-name-of-separators-alone-is-the-search-directory-itself
vectors.rationale: The join's edge, pinned because it follows from the same reading and would otherwise be a place to guess. PathAppendString collapses every run of separators to one and swallows what follows the combine's own (file_system.cpp:129-130 at stenzek/duckstation@64655818e), and Path::Combine strips what is trailing afterwards (:870-871), so PathNTSCU = "/" composes to the search directory itself — a directory where this launch wants a file, stated as obstructed rather than missing, with the requirement's file_name following the composed path rather than the raw value's empty basename. The search still speaks for the two regions the named key did not take.

vectors.name: duckstation-an-unverified-search-speaks-only-for-the-leftover-regions
vectors.rationale: The named-region machine asked without verification — the state where the caveat's regions data does its real work. The named ntsc-u image stays the group's one option, scoped and observed without hashing; the search keeps a candidate and, unverified, answers no requirement — and its firmware-search-unverified data carries exactly the regions left to it (ntsc-j, pal), never ntsc-u, which the data already answers. A reader of an unverified answer still knows which launches the candidate count speaks for.

vectors.name: duckstation-one-named-image-is-still-only-its-regions-launch
vectors.rationale: PathNTSCU names an image, the other two keys are empty, and the search keeps nothing — the directory holds no file of a size this emulator accepts. The named image is still only what a US console boots, so it stays an alternatives group of one option scoped to ntsc-u rather than flattening into a file every launch needs; ntsc-j and pal have nothing stated, and the firmware-path-names-no-file caveat says so with those two regions as data — not all three, because PathNTSCU is not empty.

vectors.name: duckstation-three-named-images-are-three-alternatives-not-three-needs
vectors.rationale: All three region keys name an image, so no region is left to the search and the search never runs — no content question, no search caveats, verify not needed. One launch reads exactly one of the keys (GetBIOSImage switches on the console region, bios.cpp:321-338 at 64655818e), so the answer is one alternatives group of three options with disjoint single regions: the ntsc-u image is missing and the other two are present, and a structured reader concludes only a US console's launch lacks its file — never that three files are needed.

vectors.name: duckstation-an-unset-search-directory-is-bios-below-the-dataroot
vectors.rationale: No SearchDirectory at all. The emulator's own LoadPathFromSettings turns an unset or empty value into the default 'bios' and hangs it off the DataRoot, so the search runs inside the emulator's own tree rather than the arrangement's BIOS root — and this machine's BIOS images, which sit in the arrangement's root, are not what this launch would find.

vectors.name: emudeck-duckstation-searches-from-the-dataroot-its-launch-picks
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck installs DuckStation as an AppImage under ~/Applications and keeps its settings under the data home (emuDeckDuckStation.sh:8), which is the DataRoot a launch outside a flatpak sandbox picks. The search directory is read from that file and the answer comes out of the arrangement's own BIOS root, the same shape RetroDECK's does — the card states keys, and where those keys live is the launch's business.

vectors.name: xemu-a-relative-bootrom-is-a-stated-launch-dependence
vectors.rationale: A firmware requirement's path is contractually the absolute observed destination, and a relative [sys.files] value has none: xemu opens it relative to its own process's working directory (system/vl.c:2983-3007 with vl.c:2527-2535 and osdep.h:645-653 at v0.8.135), which no read of this machine can establish. So the relative boot ROM stays out of the requirement list and the firmware-path-launch-dependent caveat carries the anchor as data — the key, the declared value, and the <cwd>-templated path the launcher's working directory completes — while the absolute flash image and hard disk answer exactly as before.

vectors.name: duckstation-a-case-variant-spelling-of-the-bios-keys-governs
vectors.rationale: [bios] searchdirectory and pathntscu are the [BIOS] SearchDirectory and PathNTSCU keys to the running emulator (CSimpleIniA, ini_settings_interface.h:65 at 64655818e): the search runs in the configured directory and the named NTSC-U image scopes the alternatives exactly as the canonical spellings would. An exact-case lookup would have searched the compiled default below the DataRoot and found nothing (#295).

vectors.name: pcsx2-a-case-variant-spelling-of-the-bios-keys-governs
vectors.rationale: [folders] bios and [filenames] bios are the [Folders] Bios and [Filenames] BIOS keys to the running emulator (CSimpleIniA, INISettingsInterface.h:66 at v2.6.3), so the configured BIOS directory and the chosen image govern. An exact-case lookup would have read both as unset and answered the compiled bios default with no image chosen (#295).

vectors.name: duckstation-a-per-game-settings-file-is-stated-beside-the-bios-answer
vectors.rationale: The BIOS answer is reachable from the per-game layer even though the search directory is not, and both halves belong in one statement. BIOS::GetBIOSImage reads PathNTSCJ, PathPAL and PathNTSCU through Host::GetStringSettingValue (bios.cpp:321-338), and that function reads the LAYERED interface (host.cpp:124-128) — unlike the Host::GetBase*SettingValue family beside it. So a per-game file can name a different image inside the search directory, and which image is loaded stops being a property of settings.ini alone. [BIOS] SearchDirectory itself goes through EmuFolders::LoadConfig, which is handed the base layer at every call site (settings.cpp:1964-1981), so the directory cannot move — the asymmetry is the useful part. Reachability is traced, not assumed: BootSystem installs the layer at system.cpp:1684 -> :4066 before SetBootMode at :1755 reaches LoadBIOS.

vectors.name: pcsx2-an-absolute-bios-image-name-joins-below-the-bios-directory
vectors.rationale: The [Filenames] BIOS half of #312's general question. FullpathToBios is Path::Combine(EmuFolders::Bios, BaseFilenames.Bios) (Pcsx2Config.cpp:2057-2062 at v2.6.3) — the identical combine FullpathToMcd uses for a memory card — so an absolute image name is joined BELOW the BIOS directory rather than opened where it points. atlas composed it with os.path.join, which in Python lets an absolute second argument replace the first; the same wrong outcome as the memory-card defect, reached by a quieter route, since here no code tested for an absolute value at all. The image really sits at the composed path, so the requirement is satisfied there and nowhere else.
